title: Finite-type points meet nonempty locally closed subsets of algebraic stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$. An algebraic stack over $S$ means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, representability and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and algebraic spaces are [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the field-point set and smooth-atlas topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. A point $x\in|\mathcal X|$ is of finite type if it has a representative $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$ that is locally of finite type, with $K$ a field [def-weil-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Locally of finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts with the scheme notion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $\mathcal X_{\mathrm{ft}}$ for the set of these points. For every locally closed subset $Z\subseteq|\mathcal X|$, meaning an intersection of an open subset and a closed subset, $Z\ne\varnothing$ implies $Z\cap\mathcal X_{\mathrm{ft}}\ne\varnothing$. No Jacobson, Noetherian or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $S$ or $\mathcal X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$. Write $Z=O\cap C$ with $O$ open and $C$ closed, and put $T=|p|^{-1}(Z)$. Continuity from [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open] gives $T=|p|^{-1}(O)\cap|p|^{-1}(C)$ locally closed in $|U|$. It is nonempty: choose $z\in Z$ and a field object representing it. The surjectivity convention in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] lifts this object to $U$ after a field extension; its point lies in $T$ because common field extension does not change the point class. The atlas map is representable by algebraic spaces, as required in that convention.

source.place: Tag 06G2 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points), first assertion; atlas-pullback variant using the scheme version Tag 02J4 (morphisms-lemma-enough-finite-type-points) and composition Tag 06FT (lemma-composition-finite-type).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-points-detect-open] to the scheme $U$ and the nonempty locally closed subset $T$. It supplies $u\in T$ whose canonical residue-field morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type. In particular $a$ is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This application uses the arbitrary-scheme statement of the cited lemma and needs no Jacobson or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points), first assertion, applied to the atlas scheme; finite-type points are defined by Tag 02J1 (definition-finite-type-point).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], the smooth representable morphism $p$ is locally of finite presentation and therefore locally of finite type. Regard the scheme map $a$ as a representable morphism of algebraic stacks; its chart test is the scheme notion already used in step 2. The same calculus gives that $p\circ a$ is locally of finite type. Its domain is the spectrum of the field $\kappa(u)$ and its point class is $|p|(u)$, by the composition rule of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Since $u\in T$, this class belongs to $Z$; since $p\circ a$ is a locally finite type field representative, it belongs to $\mathcal X_{\mathrm{ft}}$ by the definition in the statement. Thus $Z\cap\mathcal X_{\mathrm{ft}}$ is nonempty.
